title: check warns of an open item whose touches name a CLI facade and no module behind it, naming the module the map gives
goal: backlog.py check warns of an open item whose touches name _tools/backlog.py, _tools/kbgit.py, _tools/querylog.py or _tools/benchmarks.py and no bl_, kg_, ql_ or bench_ module, naming the module the map gives; today facade touches make items overlap by name and the check misses the real file. Narrowed on 2026-10-04: no verdict line and no new exit codes for held --overlaps (that mattered only with several concurrent sessions).

gates.question: Which map names the module behind a facade touch?
options: the facade's module prefix: backlog.py bl_, kbgit.py kg_, querylog.py ql_, benchmarks.py bench_, the warning naming the prefix glob
the subcommand registry, naming the one module that owns the command the item's text names
gates.recommendation: the facade's module prefix: backlog.py bl_, kbgit.py kg_, querylog.py ql_, benchmarks.py bench_, the warning naming the prefix glob
gates.answer: the facade's module prefix: backlog.py bl_, kbgit.py kg_, querylog.py ql_, benchmarks.py bench_, the warning naming the prefix glob

notes: Theme: overlap rules and stale touches. Evidence: backlog.py:515-549 cmd_held exits 1 for any overlap and prints no verdict; bl_plan.py:62-84 stale_touches flags only paths the tree lacks, and takes a path no commit had for one to create (kb/_self/autopilot.md in BG-rgdrjsz6, BG-2lj5x3eh, BG-fmznri7r); a held-into-cut pipe hid the exit code twice (mac-third, mac-fourth); facade touches in 5 of 9 items (mac-fourth) and a 7-item replan (mac-seventh); the docs-overlap exception the manager granted verbally is written nowhere. Relates ST-igln3v6y (section-level claims of shared docs).
